
=================================================================
#51 King Muyeol  (654 March)
Arc: The Chunchu Era · place: surabol · tone: coronation drama
Logline: For seven years the crown has sat on the Queen. The work has sat on her nephew’s table.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ For seven years the crown has sat on Queen Jinduk. The work has sat on her nephew’s table. Nobody has ever called her foolish. She’s simply outnumbered by seals.
[1] Queen Jinduk: Nephew. / When I die, do not pretend I ruled. / Say I kept the chair warm until the country was ready to admit who was already sitting in it.
[2] King Muyeol: Aunt. / You ruled the only way left to Sacred Bone — by lasting.
[3] ¶ Kangrim reads her name three times — Jinduk. Jinduk. Jinduk. — the ledger's habit before a Sacred Bone line closes.
[4] Kangrim: Majesty. / Sacred Bone ends on your breath. One question. / Did you keep the crown warm for the next hand — or keep it from cooling into a man’s?
[5] Queen Jinduk: …I kept a seat from becoming a joke. / That is all the Sacred Bone had left to do.
[6] Kangrim: Then the minutes are clean. / Walk.
[7] ── SCENE: The Harmony Council ──
[8] ¶ The Harmony Council meets to choose a king. For the first time since there was a council, there is no Sacred Bone left to choose.
[9] ¶ So the room does what rooms do with an empty chair. It offers it to the oldest man present. Alchun is High Councillor. He has been waiting seven years for this, so that he can refuse it.
[10] Councillor: High Councillor. The room asks you first.
[11] Alchun: Me? / Your servant is old, and has no virtue worth naming. / I told you lot on the wall. The chair you offered me afterward would be empty. / In virtue and standing nobody here weighs what Lord Chunchu weighs. He’s the one who can save the age.
[12] Alchun: Come now~ is there anyone who doesn’t know it will be Chunchu~~
[13] Councillor: A True Bone king. The bone has never once—
[14] Alchun: A True Bone on the throne. First since there was a throne. / …Somebody had probably better write that down.
[15] ¶ Alchun laughs the last hand up. Then everyone looks at the one man in the room who has spent his life sitting anywhere but that chair.
[16] King Muyeol: My lords. I have never once wanted to sit there.
[17] Alchun: Then sit in it, and stop making the rest of us stand.
[18] King Muyeol: This servant can find no reason to object. / Nor could anyone else.
[19] Alchun: The age of **Kim Chunchu** begins.
[20] [CARD King Muyeol]
[21] ¶ Munhee becomes queen. Years ago her sister sold her a dream on a hill. She married in disgrace, to a man with no claim to anything. Now she stands beside his throne.
[22] [CARD Munhee]
[23] Munhee: My sister sold me that dream for one silk skirt. / In hindsight she undercharged.
[24] ¶ The new king’s first council is about Baekje. It is short.
[25] Alchun: Your Majesty… even so…. / To lead the country down a road of ruin for a private grudge — that is not the act of a wise king…!
[26] King Muyeol: ….What? A private grudge? / Is that truly how you have all seen me? / An old man maddened by his daughter’s death, sharpening revenge? / How… disappointing. / I am a man looking at the thousand-year flourishing of the sacred country. / I was raised on the study of kingship from childhood…
[27] Kim Yushin: I do not know whether to fear him or admire him…. / And yet— / Kim Chunchu…
[28] ¶ That night a letter leaves Surabol for Chang’an, written in a hand that still remembers the Wei River. It begins without titles: _Zhi — I kept the appointment. Do not let the coat eat you._
[29] ── SCENE: Chang’an ──
[30] The Third Emperor: He became king. / Of course he did. / Send him horses. And tell him the dust here still has room for one more inconvenient man.
[31] ¶ Far west, the Third Emperor’s court learns a new gravity. The young woman who once waited in an anteroom now finishes sentences the emperor starts. Clerks say her influence is growing by the day. They say it softly.
[32] ── SCENE: The Crown Prince’s Rooms ──
[33] ¶ Late that night the new crown prince is still at his table, with the levy rolls for his father’s war. His wife reads them over his shoulder. She has been doing it for ten years.
[34] Jahee: Your sums are wrong. / The rice for the western forts. You carried a one.
[35] King Munmu: …Ten years, and you still say it the same way.
[36] Jahee: Ten years, and you still carry the one.
[37] ¶ **The first time she said it, he was eighteen, the quay was wet, and the brush in her hand was stolen…!**
